question: Does a monthly Labour Force Survey result describe what respondents did throughout the whole month?
generated_answer: The Labour Force Survey asks respondents about their activities during the week preceding the Sunday of the interview. You should not assume that the entire month was spent in the same activity. For example, a respondent may have been unemployed for the entire month of February, but that does not necessarily imply they were unemployed for the first 3 weeks and employed for the last week, or employed for the first 3 weeks and unemployed for the last week. How do you determine if someone is employed or unemployed? The LFS determines employment and unemployment by collecting information on the major activity of the respondent. If a person who is not working did not actively look for work during the reference week, they are counted as not in the labour force, even if they want a job. A person is considered employed if they did any work at all at their job or business. This includes not just paid employees but unpaid family workers who work at least fifteen hours a week. A person is considered unemployed if they are without work, have actively looked for work in the previous four weeks, and are available for work. The participation rate is the total civilian labour force divided by the population 15 years of age and over. How is the unemployment rate calculated? The unemployment rate is one of the simplest and most widely used labour market indicators. It is the number of unemployed divided by the total civilian labour force. What is the difference between "unemployed" and "not in the labour force"? A person is classified as unemployed if they are without work, have actively looked for work in the previous four weeks, and are available for work. A person is not in the labour force if they had not looked for work in the previous four weeks and are not available for work. Who is counted as unemployed? People are classified as unemployed if they do not have a job, have actively looked for work in the previous four weeks, and are available for work. Workers who are on a paid or unpaid leave of absence are not considered unemployed, because they have a specific job to which they are returning. Workers on layoff are not automatically counted as unemployed, because they need to be actively looking for work in order to be classified as unemployed. Is a person unemployed if they quit their job? A person is not counted as unemployed if they quit their job and they are not looking for a new one. They are counted as unemployed if they quit their job and are looking for a new one. Is a person counted as unemployed if they are waiting to be called back to a job from which they have been laid off? No. A person is not counted as unemployed if they are waiting to be called back from a temporary layoff. How is the data weighted? The LFS data are weighted using estimates of the total population aged 15 and over (the civilian, non-institutionalized population) derived from the 2011 Census of Population. These weights are first calculated for each province and territory (sub-areas) and then are adjusted to agree with the population totals by age group and gender for Canada from the 2011 Census of Population. The weights are revised based on the most recent population counts from the census, and the data are re-weighted. Why is the adjusted unemployment rate important to give a fuller picture of the economy? As Canada's labour market adjusts to global economic developments, changes in employment and unemployment are reflected in the LFS. At the same time, there are also changes in the composition of the employed and unemployed population, for example, in the age and educational characteristics. Since the adjusted unemployment rate is based on a broader definition of unemployment, it provides a better description of the unused resources in the labour market.
